packs.title: Mountain to Sea
packs.promise: Explore Rio through mountain views, living avenues and the edges of bay and ocean.

q.s: Collect a close detail, a water detail and a distant outline.
st: Choose an open pedestrian section beside Parque dos Patins and identify a safe turnaround no more than five minutes ahead.
On the short return walk, collect three descriptions: a close texture, something on the water and a distant hill or building outline. Nothing needs to be removed.
Arrange the observations from nearest to farthest and note which one changes fastest. If the distant view is obscured, record that limit.

q.s: Make a small bay portrait from the public waterfront.
st: Find an open pavement position beside the Mureta, leaving room for pedestrians and residents. Stay on the land side rather than climbing onto the wall.
Create a six-line bay sketch or six short written lines: include the water edge, one distant contour and one detail that changes while you watch.
Give your study a title based on an observed colour, movement or shape. Keep imagined details separate from what you saw.

q.s: Translate Copacabana’s pavement rhythm into a new pattern.
st: Find a clear pedestrian-side stopping place near Posto 5 where you can see a short section of the wave pavement.
Trace one repeating wave in your notebook or describe its rhythm in words. Notice where a dark band narrows and widens.
Make a new four-wave pattern on paper, changing just one thing—spacing, thickness or rhythm. Label it as your own variation. Never draw on the pavement.

packs.title: Port to Praça XV
packs.promise: Explore the port and historic centre through places of memory, public art and changing cultural spaces.

q.s: Make a small palette response to the Etnias mural.
st: Find a public viewing position facing an open section of the Etnias mural, leaving cycle and pedestrian paths clear.
Choose three visible colour relationships: a strong contrast, a quieter neighbouring pair and a repeated accent. Write the colours or make small notebook swatches.
Create your own six-shape paper pattern using those relationships. Keep it a colour response rather than copying a face or inventing a story about the people depicted.
Add the artist and mural name to your note, distinguishing the existing artwork from your own small response.

q.s: Collect how three artworks use their materials differently.
st: Enter the MAR galleries with valid admission during the open window: pay the applicable fee by credit/debit card (no cash), or present the required proof for an eligible free ticket. Check the linked MAR eligibility. Store bulky bags as directed and follow the available gallery route.
Choose three works in open displays. For each, record the artist/title from its label when available and one material or method the label supports. Leave uncertain materials uncertain.
Collect one visible difference in how each work uses surface, scale or space. Keep your description separate from any claim about the artist’s intention.
Choose the work that made you look twice and write the particular detail that changed on the second look.

q.s: Write a small future-facing response grounded in one museum display.
st: Book valid museum admission for the day and hour you will use, paying the applicable fee or selecting documented eligible free admission and bringing the required proof. Check the linked museum eligibility, arrive in that slot and follow the entry route. This afternoon starts here around noon.
In an open display outside Cosmos, choose an explanation or data presentation you can read. Record one claim exactly enough to preserve its meaning, including its date, scale or uncertainty if given.
Write a two-sentence response: a supported observation about the display, then your own clearly marked question about what might change in the future. You do not have to predict an answer.
Name the display or describe where you found it so your note can be traced back to the museum.
